clue.text: Unusually deep loving evolving

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the two words are arranged in an unusual new order

explanation.surface: A description of a deep love affair that keeps growing in strange ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something growing or changing gradually over time; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: A nervous response after Scotch perhaps could be striking

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the word for a Scotch

parts.note: a dram is a measure of whisky, such as Scotch
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone twitching nervously after downing a whisky, which looks striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic and striking both describe something vivid, eye-catching and impressive.

clue.text: Ballot victor due to get time for wife

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to get here means to receive, so time is received into the word
for means in place of, so time stands in place of wife

parts.note: owing means due, as a debt

explanation.surface: An election winner waiting for his time while his wife steps aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Replacing W with T in OWING gives OTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is the act of voting, so the noun use of the verb's -ing form matches it.

clue.text: Measure the French fever

parts.note: le is French for the
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: Taking a reading of a French patient's temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an old unit of distance of about three miles, so it is a measure of length.

clue.text: Force members to uphold the law

definitions.text: Force members to uphold the law

parts.words: Force members to uphold the law
parts.note: the members of a police force are the people whose job is enforcing the law

explanation.surface: Someone compelling members of a group to obey the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as a verb, compelling members, but it is the noun: a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers of a constabulary, called a force in Britain, are the people charged with keeping the law.

clue.text: Beginning to drive in VW is hard for one in tank?

indicators.note: in says the first letter of drive goes inside the car model

parts.note: the Golf is a Volkswagen car model

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word drive

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Learning to drive a Volkswagen is tough for someone in an army tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tank' suggests a military vehicle beside the car, but it is a fish tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfish is the classic pet kept in a glass bowl or aquarium, an example of a tank dweller.

clue.text: Reportedly hoard money

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the word for a hoard is said aloud

parts.note: a cache is a hidden hoard or store

explanation.surface: A rumour about someone squirrelling away their savings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in notes and coins, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Success in hoax investigation

parts.note: a con is a swindle or hoax
a quest is a search or inquiry

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a fraud that turns out well.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a victory or triumph, a winning of something, hence a success.

clue.text: Partly suspect rumoured range of opinions?

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some doubtful gossip, giving a selection of views.
explanation.definitionFit: A political spectrum is the full scale of views from one extreme to the other.

clue.text: Work with university colleague, in fact

parts.note: to act is to work or function
an ally is a partner or colleague on one's side

explanation.surface: Someone noting that a co-worker at the university really does work alongside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbs meaning really or as a matter of truth.

clue.text: Sofa, not posh, with more space to sit?

indicators.note: not says the letter standing for posh is left out of the word for a sofa

parts.note: a lounger is a couch or reclining seat
U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A furniture comparison: a humbler sofa that gives you more room to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a longer seat offers more room along its length, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of greater length has more room along it, so a longer bench seats more people.

clue.text: Reveal new part of speech in a church

indicators.note: in says the pieces for new and the part of speech are placed inside a and church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a noun is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: A vicar unveiling a fresh section of a sermon in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal news is to make it known publicly, which is to proclaim or declare it.

clue.text: Leading estate, this could make the papers!

definitions.text: Leading estate, this could make the papers!

parts.words: Leading estate, this could make the papers
parts.note: the word placed in front of estate gives the phrase for the press, which makes the newspapers

explanation.surface: A grand country estate whose story might hit the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fourth Estate is the press: put this word before 'estate' and you have the people who make the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fourth Estate is a traditional name for journalism and the newspapers, after the three estates of the realm.

clue.text: Plans found in junk mail returned

indicators.note: returned means the word for junk mail is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk email

explanation.surface: Someone's plans turning up among junk mail sent back to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are drawn plans of an area, as in a street plan of a town.

clue.text: Affirm boast about unfinished government order

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for boast goes round the shortened order

parts.note: to prate is to talk boastfully or idly

indicators.note: unfinished says the order loses its final letter

parts.note: an edict is an official decree issued by a government

explanation.surface: Bragging about a government decree that was never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the boast round the order, and 'unfinished' drops the order's final T. Predicate as a verb is a formal word, seen mostly in logic and philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate something is to assert or declare it as true, a formal sense of affirming.

clue.text: Round capital city, cold and extremely tense atmosphere

indicators.note: round says the letters for cold and the ends of tense surround the city

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: extremely picks the two extreme letters of the word tense

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A tense, chilly mood in and around a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate is used figuratively for the prevailing mood or atmosphere, as in a climate of fear.

clue.text: Drink large mead one served up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

indicators.note: served up suggests the letters are dished out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pouring out a big glass of mead for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink flavoured with lemons, an example of a beverage.

clue.text: Publication that may include explosive material

definitions.meaning: a periodical such as a glossy weekly
a store for ammunition or gunpowder, or the cartridge holder in a gun

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a periodical and an arms store or chamber holding cartridges.

clue.text: Quarrel after motor crashed this time yesterday?

indicators.note: after says the quarrel comes behind the rearranged letters
crashed says the letters of motor are smashed into a new order

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: An argument following a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: seen from yesterday, today was the day to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking yesterday, the present day would have been the day after, so it fits with a question mark.

clue.text: Beats unusual myth penned by gardeners

indicators.note: penned by says the rearranged letters are enclosed by the gardeners

parts.note: the RHS is the Royal Horticultural Society, Britain's gardening charity

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of myth are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd legend written down by members of a gardening society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles myth, and 'penned by' sets the result inside the Royal Horticultural Society's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Beats are the regular pulses of music, which together form its rhythm patterns.

clue.text: Chose last of ones voted for

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word ones

parts.note: elected means voted into office

explanation.surface: Choosing the final candidate among those who were voted in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past tense verbs meaning picked out from a group in preference to others.

clue.text: Formerly concealed content

indicators.note: content means what is contained inside the word concealed

explanation.surface: Something that used to be hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as a noun, the contents, not 'happy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at some time in the past, as in he was once a teacher.

clue.text: Inattentive — shake please!

indicators.note: shake says the letters of please are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asking to be nudged awake because they have drifted off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping, or figuratively not alert, is paying no attention.

clue.text: Cover emerging from hassle eventually

indicators.note: emerging from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Protection that finally appears after some bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A record or book sleeve is a protective outer case, a kind of cover or jacket.

clue.text: Fruit's extremely arresting dull surface

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the word for extremely holds the other piece

parts.note: too means excessively or extremely
a mat finish is a dull, non-shiny surface

explanation.surface: A fruit whose skin is strikingly dull rather than glossy.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically this salad staple is a fruit, the berry of the plant; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Wind up backing deficit hidden by disreputable resort?

indicators.note: hidden by says the reversed piece is tucked inside the disreputable resort

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club

indicators.note: backing means the word for a deficit is read backwards

parts.note: a loss is a deficit or shortfall

explanation.surface: A business in the red, hidden away in a shady establishment, about to fold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the deficit round, and 'hidden by' tucks it inside the seedy dive. 'Wind up' here is the business sense of closing down.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a company or partnership is to formally bring it to an end, to terminate it.

clue.text: Get basic new bra with no restraints, it's more comfortable

indicators.note: restraints are the things bounding each word, so these four words lose their outside letters

explanation.surface: Advice to buy a simple new bra without underwiring for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no restraints' strips the first and last letters from Get, basic, new and bra, leaving E, ASI, E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less difficult or more relaxed is comparatively comfortable; the 'it's' frames the comparative adjective.

clue.text: Humiliation, lacking a cellar

indicators.note: lacking says the letter a goes missing from the word for humiliation

parts.note: abasement is humiliation or degradation

explanation.surface: Being relegated to the cellar as a humiliating experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey below ground level, much like a cellar.

clue.text: Nothing more than a pool

definitions.meaning: as an adjective it means only or simply
a lake or pond, a poetic word

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the adjective for only, the other the old word for a lake or pond.

clue.text: Wholesale whiskey I had before English meal

indicators.note: before says these pieces come ahead of those for English and meal

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I'd is short for I had
a spread is a lavish meal laid out on a table

explanation.surface: A drinker recalling a whisky before a big English dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale used as an adjective means extensive or indiscriminate, sweeping across everything.
